stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A sports scientist selected 200 athletes at random from the 1,200 athletes registered in a regional youth soccer league. Of the sampled athletes, 35% scored below a recommended threshold on a hamstring flexibility test. Based on the sample, the estimated proportion of the league's athletes who would score below the threshold is 35%, with an associated margin of error of 4%.
choices: It is plausible that between 62 and 78 of the league's 1,200 athletes would score below the threshold.
It is plausible that between 372 and 468 of the league's 1,200 athletes would score below the threshold.
It is plausible that between 31% and 39% of the 200 sampled athletes scored below the threshold.
It is certain that more than 372 of the league's 1,200 athletes would score below the threshold.
explanation: The interval for the league proportion is $35\% \pm 4\%$, so 31% to 39%. The conclusion is about the league, which has 1,200 athletes, so you convert using 1,200: $0.31 \times 1{,}200 = 372$ and $0.39 \times 1{,}200 = 468$. So it is plausible that between 372 and 468 of the league's athletes would score below the threshold.

A.why: You found 31% to 39% correctly but multiplied by the sample size, 200, instead of the league size, 1,200. That gives $0.31 \times 200 = 62$ and $0.39 \times 200 = 78$, which are counts for the sample. The claim is about the 1,200 athletes in the league.

C.why: You applied the interval to the sample. The sample's percent is known exactly: 35% of the 200 sampled athletes, which is 70 athletes. The margin of error describes uncertainty about the league proportion, not about the sample.

D.why: You used the right lower bound but turned it into a one-sided, certain claim. The interval only makes values from 372 to 468 plausible. It does not make any count certain, and it says nothing about counts above 468.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A precast plant made 300 concrete deck panels for a single bridge. Each panel's design compressive strength is 40 megapascals (MPa). An inspector tested 25 of these panels, selected at random. Based on the results, the inspector estimated that the mean compressive strength of the 300 panels is 3.5 MPa above the design strength, with an associated margin of error of 2.0 MPa.
choices: The mean compressive strength of the bridge's 300 panels is plausibly between 41.5 MPa and 45.5 MPa.
The mean compressive strength of the bridge's 300 panels is plausibly between 38.0 MPa and 42.0 MPa.
The compressive strength of each of the bridge's 300 panels is plausibly between 41.5 MPa and 45.5 MPa.
The mean compressive strength of all panels made at the plant is plausibly between 41.5 MPa and 45.5 MPa.
explanation: The estimated mean is $40 + 3.5 = 43.5$ MPa. Applying the margin of error gives $43.5 - 2.0 = 41.5$ MPa and $43.5 + 2.0 = 45.5$ MPa. The interval describes the mean of the population that was sampled, which is the 300 panels made for this bridge.

B.why: You applied the margin of error to the design strength, $40 \pm 2.0$, instead of to the estimated mean. The estimate is 3.5 MPa above design, so the interval is centered at 43.5 MPa, not 40 MPa.

C.why: You did the arithmetic correctly but applied the interval to individual panels. A margin of error describes where the mean plausibly lies. Individual panels can be well above or below that range.

D.why: You did the arithmetic correctly but extended the conclusion beyond the population that was sampled. The 25 panels were drawn only from the 300 made for this bridge, so the result says nothing about the plant's other panels.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A textile museum holds 1,200 quilts made in a single county during the 1800s. A conservator randomly selected 80 of these quilts and found that 35% of the selected quilts contain at least one indigo-dyed fabric, with an associated margin of error of 5%.
choices: It is plausible that between 415 and 425 of the museum's 1,200 quilts contain indigo-dyed fabric.
It is plausible that between 360 and 480 of the museum's 1,200 quilts contain indigo-dyed fabric.
It is plausible that between 30% and 40% of all quilts made in the 1800s contain indigo-dyed fabric.
It is plausible that between 24 and 32 of the 80 selected quilts contain indigo-dyed fabric.
explanation: The plausible range for the museum's proportion is 35% − 5% = 30% to 35% + 5% = 40%. Apply that range to the 1,200 quilts the sample was drawn from: 0.30 × 1,200 = 360 and 0.40 × 1,200 = 480.

A.why: You took the margin of error as 5 quilts on either side of 420. The margin is 5 percentage points, which is 60 quilts out of 1,200.

C.why: You stretched the result to every quilt made in the 1800s. The sample came only from this museum's 1,200 quilts from one county, so the conclusion only covers those quilts.

D.why: You applied the interval to the sample. The conservator already counted the 80 quilts: exactly 35%, or 28, contain indigo. The margin of error describes uncertainty about the 1,200, not the 80.

stem: Which of the following is the most plausible conclusion?
stimulus: A sound archive holds 600 recorded performances of a certain piano sonata. A musicologist randomly selected 50 of these recordings and timed the first movement of each. The mean duration of the first movement for the selected recordings was 9.4 minutes, with an associated margin of error of 0.6 minutes.
choices: Every one of the archive's 600 recordings has a first movement lasting between 8.8 and 10.0 minutes.
The mean first-movement duration for the 50 selected recordings is between 8.8 and 10.0 minutes.
The mean first-movement duration for the archive's 600 recordings is between 8.8 and 10.0 minutes.
The mean first-movement duration for all recordings ever made of the sonata is between 8.8 and 10.0 minutes.
explanation: The interval runs from 9.4 − 0.6 = 8.8 to 9.4 + 0.6 = 10.0 minutes. It estimates the mean of the population that was sampled, which is the archive's 600 recordings.

A.why: You applied the interval to individual recordings. It estimates the population mean. Single performances can be much faster or slower than 8.8 to 10.0 minutes.

B.why: You applied the interval to the sample. The 50 recordings were timed, so their mean is known exactly: 9.4 minutes. The uncertainty is about the 600.

D.why: You extended the result beyond the archive. Only this archive's 600 recordings could be selected, so recordings outside it were never sampled.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A weather station has a 400-day record of daily rainfall. A meteorologist randomly selected 50 days from this record and found that 30% of the selected days had at least 1 millimeter of rainfall, with an associated margin of error of 10%.
choices: It is plausible that between 80 and 160 of the 400 recorded days had less than 1 millimeter of rainfall.
It is plausible that between 270 and 290 of the 400 recorded days had less than 1 millimeter of rainfall.
It is plausible that between 35 and 45 of the 50 selected days had less than 1 millimeter of rainfall.
It is plausible that between 240 and 320 of the 400 recorded days had less than 1 millimeter of rainfall.
explanation: The days with at least 1 mm make up 20% to 40% of the record, so the days with less than 1 mm make up 60% to 80%. Out of 400 days, that is 0.60 × 400 = 240 to 0.80 × 400 = 320.

A.why: You found the interval for days with at least 1 mm (20% to 40% of 400) and stopped. The choices ask about days with less than 1 mm, which is the complement.

B.why: You took the margin as 10 days on either side of 280. The margin is 10 percentage points, which is 40 days out of 400.

C.why: You applied the interval to the sample. The 50 selected days were observed directly: exactly 35 had less than 1 mm. The margin of error describes the 400-day record.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A sky survey catalogued 900 pulsating variable stars in one field of view. An astronomer randomly selected 64 of these stars and measured their pulsation periods. The mean period of the selected stars was 5.2 days, with an associated margin of error of 0.4 days.
choices: It is plausible that the mean period of the 900 catalogued stars is between 4.8 and 5.6 days.
It is not possible that the mean period of the 900 catalogued stars is less than 4.8 days.
It is plausible that most of the 900 catalogued stars have periods between 4.8 and 5.6 days.
It is plausible that the mean period of the 900 catalogued stars is between 5.0 and 5.4 days.
explanation: Compute 5.2 − 0.4 = 4.8 and 5.2 + 0.4 = 5.6. The interval gives plausible values for the mean period of the 900 stars that were sampled.

B.why: You read the bottom of the interval as a hard limit. A margin of error gives plausible values. It does not make values outside the interval impossible.

C.why: You applied the interval to individual stars. It estimates the mean period, and says nothing about how many single stars have periods in that range.

D.why: You treated 0.4 days as the full width of the interval and split it in half. The margin is added to and subtracted from the estimate in full.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A county wetland survey lists 3,000 ponds. Ecologists randomly selected 150 of these ponds and found a nonnative snail in 54% of them, with an associated margin of error of 6%.
choices: It must be true that more than 1,500 of the county's ponds contain the snail.
It is plausible that between 1,440 and 1,800 of the state's ponds contain the snail.
It is plausible that fewer than 1,500 of the county's ponds contain the snail.
It is plausible that between 72 and 90 of the sampled ponds contain the snail.
explanation: The plausible range is 54% − 6% = 48% to 54% + 6% = 60% of the county's 3,000 ponds, which is 1,440 to 1,800 ponds. Values from 1,440 up to 1,499 lie inside that range, so fewer than 1,500 (fewer than half) is plausible. The estimate of 54% does not rule it out.

A.why: You saw that 54% is above half and treated the estimate as exact. The interval reaches down to 48%, so the data don't guarantee a majority.

B.why: You got the right counts but attached them to the wrong population. Only the county's ponds were sampled, so nothing can be concluded about ponds elsewhere in the state.

D.why: You applied the interval to the sample. The 150 ponds were checked directly, so exactly 81 contain the snail. The margin of error describes the 3,000.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A print archive holds 1,100 color woodblock prints, 480 of which were made after 1890. A curator randomly selected 40 of the 480 post-1890 prints and counted the separate color blocks used for each. The mean for the selected prints was 7.5 blocks per print, with an associated margin of error of 1.5 blocks.
choices: It is plausible that each of the 480 post-1890 prints used between 6 and 9 color blocks.
It is plausible that the mean for the 480 post-1890 prints is between 6 and 9 blocks per print.
It is plausible that the mean for all 1,100 archived prints is between 6 and 9 blocks per print.
The mean for the 480 post-1890 prints is exactly 7.5 blocks per print.
explanation: Compute 7.5 − 1.5 = 6 and 7.5 + 1.5 = 9. The sample was drawn only from the 480 post-1890 prints, so the interval estimates the mean for those prints.

A.why: You applied the interval to every individual print. It estimates the mean. Individual prints can use far fewer or far more blocks.

C.why: You extended the result to the whole archive. The 620 prints made in or before 1890 could never be selected, so the conclusion can't cover them.

D.why: You treated the sample mean as the population mean. 7.5 is only an estimate, and the margin of error shows that the true mean could plausibly be anywhere from 6 to 9.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A health department randomly selected 200 of a city's 40,000 adult residents and recorded each person's daily fiber intake. The mean intake for the selected adults was 21 grams per day, with an associated margin of error of 3 grams per day. A dietary guideline recommends 25 grams per day.
choices: Every adult in the city plausibly falls short of the 25-gram guideline by between 1 and 7 grams per day.
The mean intake of the 200 selected adults plausibly falls short of 25 grams by between 1 and 7 grams per day.
The mean intake of the city's adults falls short of the 25-gram guideline by exactly 4 grams per day.
The mean intake of the city's adults plausibly falls short of 25 grams by between 1 and 7 grams per day.
explanation: The plausible city mean runs from 21 − 3 = 18 to 21 + 3 = 24 grams. Its shortfall from 25 grams therefore runs from 25 − 24 = 1 to 25 − 18 = 7 grams, and that range describes the mean of the city's adults.

A.why: You applied the interval to every individual. It describes the mean intake. Some residents may meet the guideline and others may fall far below it.

B.why: You applied the interval to the sample. The 200 adults were measured, so their mean is exactly 21 grams and their shortfall is exactly 4 grams.

C.why: You treated the estimate as exact. A shortfall of 4 grams comes from the sample mean, and the margin of error widens it to 1 to 7 grams.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A seed lot contains 20,000 wheat seeds. An agronomist randomly selected 400 seeds from the lot and found that 85% of the selected seeds germinated under standard test conditions, with an associated margin of error of 4%. The seller claims that at least 90% of the seeds in the lot will germinate under these conditions.
choices: It is plausible that between 16,200 and 17,800 seeds in the lot would germinate under these conditions.
It is plausible that at least 90% of the seeds in the lot would germinate under these conditions.
It is plausible that between 324 and 356 of the 400 selected seeds germinated under these conditions.
It is plausible that between 16,320 and 17,680 seeds in the lot would germinate under these conditions.
explanation: The plausible range is 85% − 4% = 81% to 85% + 4% = 89% of the lot. As counts, that is 0.81 × 20,000 = 16,200 to 0.89 × 20,000 = 17,800.

B.why: You noticed that 90% is close to the estimate but didn't check it against the interval. The interval ends at 89%, so the seller's claim is not supported by the data.

C.why: You applied the interval to the sample. The 400 seeds were tested, so exactly 340 germinated. The margin of error describes the 20,000-seed lot.

D.why: You took 4% of the estimated 17,000 seeds (680) as the margin. The margin is 4 percentage points of the whole lot: 0.04 × 20,000 = 800 seeds.
